title: What makes a racy frame racy?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 176 cm (5’ 9.3”) high rider, according to manufacturer’s charts.



Racy bike frames have a combination of low stack, short front-center, high head tube angles, and low trail




















Racy frames have short reach, relative to rowdy frames








Racy frames have short chainstays (and rear-center), relative to relaxed frames








Racy frames can have low seat tube angles








Racy frames tend to have short front and rear centers. Relaxed frames tend to have long front and rear centers. So both racy and relaxed frames have low front-center:rear-center but for different reasons.

p9







Stack:Reach and bottom brack drop aren’t really related to relaxedness

title: The three gravel styles: racy, relaxed, and rowdy
text:

Which bikes are racy? rowdy? relaxed?




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model in the plot.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note




The ternary scores are the projections of the centered, scaled data onto the style (Racy, Relaxed, Rowdy) axes.
There are several ways to construct a style axis. The ternary plot uses the 2nd of these two ways:

the vector of differences from the centroid to the style mean of the centered, scaled data.
the vector of correlation coefficients between the style classification (1 is “in style” and 0 is “out of style”) and each measure.

The input data is the ML subset of bikes that fit a 176 cm rider

title: What makes a relaxed frame relaxed?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 176 cm (5’ 9.3”) high rider, according to manufacturer’s charts.



Relaxed bike frames have a combination of high stack, short reach, and long chain stays












By themselves, stack and reach aren’t really related to relaxedness












Headtube angle, seattube angle, bottom bracket drop, and trail aren’t really related to relaxedness

title: How does a suspension fork change bike geometry?
text:
Model




















How does a suspension change bike geometry?




Cane Creek Invert has two models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel. Both models have 45 mm offset
Rockshox Rudy has four models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 51 mm offset.
Fox 32 TC Factory has four models: 40 (435.5 mm axle-crown) mm and 50 (445.5 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 50 mm offset.









Note




The suspension fork length is based on 10% sag: fork_length - 0.1*travel

title: Gravel Bike Geometry Project
text:
Start here
The Which bikes are racy/rowdy/relaxed? page contains interactive plots for all gravel bike models in the database. Click on the points for finding bikes in the style you’re seeking.











A little deeper
The What makes a rowdy frame rowdy? and What makes a relaxed frame relaxed? pages are full of plots showing which frame measures are most correlated with a style, and which aren’t.


Into the weeds
The Gravel 2D page contains interactive, 2D scatter plots of different pairs of frame geometry measures for all gravel bike models and frame sizes in the database.











A view from afar
The What is Gravel Style? page compares gravel bikes in the database to Road Race, Road Endurance, Cyclocross, and XC Mountain bikes.











The classification
The Gravel Tree page contains a tree diagram showing the relative similarity in frame geometry among all gravel bikes in the database and the clustering of the models into three major styles.









The Gravel Table page contains a table of the classification of all gravel bike models in the database into All-road, Endurance, and Trail categories.











Also, check out the Gravel Stories
